question: Two days after delivery, a 4300-g (9-lb 8-oz) newborn has difficulty feeding and has become increasingly lethargic. His cry has become weak. He was born at term. His mother has a history of intravenous drug use. His temperature is 36.4°C (96.5°F), pulse is 170/min, respirations are 62/min, and blood pressure is 70/48 mm Hg. Examination shows midfacial hypoplasia, diaphoresis, and tremor of the lower extremities. Macroglossia is present. There are folds in the posterior auricular cartilage. The left lower extremity is larger than the right lower extremity. Abdominal examination shows an umbilical hernia. The liver is palpated 4 cm below the right costal margin. Neurological examination shows decreased tone in all extremities. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Newborn exhibits lethargy and weak cry" -> "Possible signs of withdrawal or metabolic disturbance" -> "Mother has history of intravenous drug use" -> "Risk of neonatal abstinence syndrome or opioid exposure" -> "Assess for hypoglycemia due to poor feeding" -> "Administer glucose" -> "Improved energy levels and feeding ability" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Newborn presents with diaphoresis and tremors" -> "Indicates possible withdrawal symptoms" -> "Mother's drug use raises concern for opioid exposure" -> "Weak cry and lethargy suggest possible respiratory depression" -> "Administer naloxone" -> "Reversal of respiratory depression" -> "Improved neurological status" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Newborn has macroglossia and midfacial hypoplasia" -> "Possible congenital syndrome or drug exposure effects" -> "Lethargy and poor feeding indicate metabolic issues" -> "Consider hypoglycemia as a cause" -> "Administer glucose" -> "Increased blood sugar levels" -> "Improved feeding and alertness" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Newborn shows signs of dehydration and hypotension" -> "Blood pressure is low at 70/48 mm Hg" -> "Possible need for fluid resuscitation" -> "Administer -> 3%

CHAIN: "Newborn has umbilical hernia and hepatomegaly" -> "Indicates possible metabolic disorder or congenital issue" -> "Weak cry and lethargy suggest systemic involvement" -> "Consider infection due to poor feeding" -> "Administer ampicillin and gentamicin" -> "Coverage for possible sepsis" -> 65%
analysis: The newborn presents with signs suggestive of neonatal withdrawal syndrome, likely due to the mother's history of intravenous drug use. The lethargy, weak cry, diaphoresis, tremors, and macroglossia are consistent with opioid exposure. Naloxone is an opioid antagonist that can reverse the effects of opioid toxicity and is the most appropriate intervention in this case.
